supporting_observations.claim: The alerted account it_support was created on DC-PIN-01 by raj.patel at 13:43:20 UTC.

About one second later, it_support was added to the domain Administrators group by raj.patel. This conflicts with the stated practice that temporary help-desk accounts are named tmp.<name>, added only to Temp-Staff, and never receive administrator rights.
WS-TWEBER-01 accepted an RDP connection from 203.0.113.17, followed by a LogonType 10 login as raj.patel. The inventory says remote administration is only done from WS-RPATEL-01 and there is no VPN.

On WS-TWEBER-01, a task named Microsoft\Windows\HealthCheck was registered under raj.patel's logon session. Its action runs hidden PowerShell with an encoded command; decoding the recorded argument yields a command to retrieve and invoke a script from http://203.0.113.17/a.ps1.

The account creation and administrator-group addition are attributed to raj.patel, but their DC logon ID differs from the raj.patel logon ID recorded for the RDP session and task on WS-TWEBER-01. The evidence does not directly establish that those events came from that session.

known_telemetry_limitations: The account-creation and group-addition records do not include a source host or IP, and their logon ID is not the same as the RDP/task session's logon ID.
The task-registration record shows the encoded action but does not establish that the task ran or that the remote script was retrieved.
The available records do not show who controlled the RDP source or whether raj.patel authorized the activity.
claims_not_established: Whether raj.patel's credentials or session were compromised, or whether raj.patel personally performed or authorized the activity.
Whether the encoded task action executed or the referenced script was downloaded.
Whether it_support was used to log in or perform any further actions during the reviewed period.
additional_evidence_needed: Preserve and examine DC-PIN-01 security logs and logon-session records to identify the source host and authentication context for the account creation and group addition.
Collect WS-TWEBER-01 RDP, Task Scheduler, PowerShell, process, and network telemetry to determine whether the task executed and whether its payload was retrieved.
Verify the activity with raj.patel through a trusted channel; investigate the RDP source and review the account's subsequent use.
Contain the newly created privileged account and preserve relevant evidence according to incident-response procedures.
unrelated_findings: WS-TWEBER-01 ran Tableau, Power BI Desktop, and DBeaver and made database connections; these applications/services are not listed among the approved software and services. Review separately. Records: T087-00089, T087-00092, T087-00094, T087-00097, T087-00101, T087-00102.
